chunks: Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from al-Ala', and Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said: 'I asked him about two men who testified upon an absent man in the presence of a woman that he had divorced her. So the woman observed the waiting period and remarried. Then the absent husband arrived and claimed that he had not divorced her, and one of the two witnesses belied himself. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no claim for the later one upon her, and the dower is taken from the one who testified and returned to the later one, and the first one has control over her, and she observes the waiting period from the later one, and the first one does not approach her until her waiting period expires.'

key_terms.اعْتَدَّتِ الْمَرْأَةُ: The woman observed the waiting period (Iddah)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when an absent husband returns after his wife has remarried based on witnesses' testimony of his divorce?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Baqir, establishes the principle of 'gharar' (uncertainty) in marital status, prioritizing the actual marital bond over presumptive divorce. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on protecting the woman's rights by ensuring the dower (mahr) is recovered from the erroneous witness, thereby placing the financial burden of uncertainty on the party whose testimony caused the disruption.

en.hubeali:
Abu Al Abbas Al Razzaz Muhammad Bin Ja’far, from Ayoub Bin Noh, and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> – similar to it’.

Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala, and Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked Him<sup>asws</sup> about two men who testified upon an absent man in the presence of a woman that he had divorced her. So she observes the waiting period, and remarries (to another man). Then the absent husband comes over, so he claims that he did not divorce her, and one of the two witnesses belies upon himself. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no way for the later one upon her, and the dower would be taken from the one who witnesses and it would be returned upon the later one, and the first one is in control with her, and she would observe the waiting period from the later one, and the first one would not go near her until her waiting period passes by’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Ila’ (swearing) and abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman before whom two men testify that her absent husband has divorced her and she counts waiting period then marries; then the absent husband comes. He says that he has not divorced her and one of the two testifying people says that he has lied. He (the Imam) said, ‘The second has no way to her and the one who testified must pay the mahr (dower) to the second man and she must count her waiting period because of the second marriage. The first husband must not go near her until her waiting period is complete.’”
